content_preview.title: Tulane Physicists Explain Why Gold Resists Tarnishing, Finding Surface Atoms Rearrange to Choke Off Oxidation
content_preview.summary: A Physical Review Letters study finds gold's surface atoms reconstruct into denser patterns that slow oxidation by a billion to a trillion times.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Gold jewelry can stay bright for centuries while other metals corrode within years, and a new study from Tulane University offers an explanation grounded in atomic-scale physics rather than gold's famous unreactivity alone. According to [ScienceDaily](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/07/260710003511.htm), researchers found that atoms on gold's surface reorganize themselves into protective configurations that suppress oxidation by a factor of a billion to a trillion.
